reason: The FAA airport file lists open facilities only; the airport-data README says so.
Altitude of an airborne VOR receiver checkpoint. The FAA publishes only ground checkpoints this cycle; kept so an airborne one is not published without its altitude.
Every published VOR receiver checkpoint is a ground checkpoint this cycle; the navaid-data README says so.
Every remaining fan marker has an elliptical pattern; the Navaid TSDoc says so.

No FAA record publishes a direction for a DME/DME/IRU MEA (the AWY and CSV direction columns are blank). Kept so a directional value is not read as applying both ways if the FAA starts publishing one.
Every airway segment that publishes an RNP value publishes 1.0 nm this cycle.

Class A and the area-based Class E5, E6 and E7 airspace have no associated airport, and three Class D and one Class E4 area are US portions of Canadian control zones; the airspace-data README says so.
R-2535B publishes a 100,000 ft ceiling, above the 99,999 ft sentinel for unlimited; carried as published and documented in the airspace-data README.
No CIFP leg publishes a true course this cycle. Kept so a true course is not read as magnetic if one is published.
The transition altitude is 18,000 ft throughout US airspace.
